findings.title: Daily .at() job with a timezone runs twice the day after a spring-forward when its time falls in the DST gap
A zero or negative interval makes do() loop forever instead of raising
Hourly .at() jobs with a timezone skip one run at the fall-back transition
repr() of a job that has no unit yet raises TypeError
until() with a timezone-aware datetime fails with a bare comparison TypeError
No security policy or automated security scanning
A job that raises is never rescheduled: it re-runs on every tick and starves the jobs due after it
Calling do() again on the same Job registers it a second time, so it runs twice per due time
Two time models: interval jobs use naive local time, at(tz) jobs compute in pytz and are flattened back to naive local time
No clock seam: the wall clock is read directly in nine places, so time can only be controlled by replacing datetime.datetime globally
Job writes itself into Scheduler's job list, and the module keeps a global default scheduler with a live alias of its list
The shipped type hints leave the fluent builder untyped and mistype at()'s tz argument
Units and weekdays are plain strings and invalid configurations are representable until do() or run time
The error contract is inconsistent across similar mistakes
pytz is hard-wired as the only timezone backend
Unit handling is spread over repeated string comparisons, so adding a unit touches many places
Package metadata is declared twice, in setup.py and pyproject.toml, with differing license text
A few garbled comments, cryptic helper names and a stale todo in the core module
Job.at is an 89-line, complexity-25 function that branches on the unit in three separate passes
The seven weekday properties are copy-pasted blocks that differ only in the day name
Failure paths are untested: no test makes a job raise, uses a zero or negative interval, or reschedules at the gap-adjusted DST run
test_time_range relies on unseeded randomness
Timezone support does not accept the standard library's zoneinfo objects
Two validation messages misstate the problem: an unfilled {} placeholder and an inverted to() range message
The README quickstart crashes after its own install step: its timezone line needs pytz, which pip install schedule does not install
examples.rst states the wrong first run for every(5).hours.at("20:30"): 07:20:30, not 06:20:30
The fall-back example in timezones.rst repeats the spring-forward wording
The API reference omits repeat() and the exception classes, and lists CancelJob as an exception
Some examples do not run as written: snippets without imports and until() examples with dates in the past
The documented test command cannot start: the unpinned pytest-flake8 plugin breaks pytest's plugin loading
The documented dev setup fails on Python 3.13: the black==20.8b1 pin needs typed-ast, which does not build there
Contributor docs skip tox, which is what CI runs, and there is no contributing guide or agent instructions
The documented release steps fail as written: the build step needs the 'build' package, which the given install line does not install
Releases are manual: the version is hand-edited in two files and uploaded from a maintainer's machine
CI has no lint step or coverage threshold, and its tool versions are unpinned, so runs are not reproducible
Only Linux is tested although the package declares OS Independent, and the test module cannot run on Windows
Packaging metadata uses a license form that setuptools stops supporting after 2027-02-18, with an unbounded setuptools requirement
Dev tooling is unpinned and unlocked except for a 2020 black pre-release with published advisories, and nothing automates updates
CI runs on old action majors and keeps end-of-life Pythons 3.7-3.9 in its matrix
No __all__ or __version__: the public surface is everything importable, including stdlib modules
No deprecation policy or mechanism for retiring API
No thread-safety contract: the background-thread recipe shares an unsynchronized scheduler without saying what is safe
